Frequently Asked Questions

What makes a second AC replacement different from the first in a Mauldin home?

The ductwork. By a second replacement the ducts have served as long as the house, and leakage or undersized returns will throttle new equipment exactly as they throttled the old. Testing static pressure and sealing or correcting the runs first protects the value of the new system.

How do I know when repiping beats another leak repair?

Track frequency and spread. One leak is a repair; leaks appearing at different points across the system mean the material itself is failing, and each patch buys less time. A whole-home assessment prices the repiping so the comparison is real numbers against a known repair pattern.

Our split-level has never cooled evenly. Is that fixable without new equipment?

Usually, yes. Balancing corrects modest unevenness, and zoning with dampers and per-level thermostats solves the structural version of the problem. Equipment replacement only enters the conversation if the diagnostic shows the unit itself is failing or badly missized.

Are the original outlets in my older Mauldin house actually a safety issue?

They can be. Ungrounded receptacles, absent GFCI protection near water, and worn contacts that grip plugs loosely each carry real risk, and all three are common in original installations. An electrician can update the highest-priority locations first, which puts most of the protection in place quickly.

Which nearby communities do you also serve?

Simpsonville, Five Forks, and Fountain Inn share Mauldin’s routes, and the chat team can confirm any Golden Strip address in minutes.
